newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Cathay plans HK$20 bln capex in 2-3 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Cathay plans HK$20 bln capex in 2-3 yrs.

text.p: Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd plans total capital expenditure of nearly HK$20 billion for the coming two to three years, managing director David Turnbull told a news conference on Wednesday.
"Over the next couple of years we shall be spending approximately HK$8 billion at Chep Lap Kok in various facilities including our own headquarters," Turnbull said.
The airline will spend roughly half of that sum, US$450 million, on its headquarters at Hong Kong's new international airport at Chep Lap Kok, he said.
The airport will open with one runway in April 1998, and a second runway is due to open at the end of that year.
In addition, the airline is renewing its fleet.
"We shall be taking delivery of aircraft up to the middle of 1999 at a value of around HK$10 billion," said Turnbull.
The group currently has firm orders for seven Boeing B777-300s, two Airbus A330-300s and six A340-300s.
It has options on a further 25 aircraft for delivery from 1999 to 2003, while four aircraft are due to be taken out of service through 2003.
Turnbull said the airline assumed it would need to move all its facilities "overnight" to the new airport when it opened from around the current Kai Tak airport.
The company was working out the logistics of the move, but could not at this date estimate the cost involved.
"As you can imagine it is a major exercise, a military operation," he added.
